acceptance_criteria.criterion: On first run with old flat layout, all depth-1 project directories are moved to {ledgerRoot}/{repoName}/{slug}/
Projects without repository_name in .meta.json are moved to {ledgerRoot}/unknown/{slug}/
Calling migrateToNamespacedLayout() a second time makes no changes (skips when storage_version >= 2)
withLock is never called with ledgerRoot — the .migration-in-progress sentinel file + synchronous pre-yield timing is used instead
If an individual directory move fails, the original directory is left untouched and the error is surfaced; the storage_version flag is not written
{ledgerRoot}/.migration-state.json is written only after all moves complete successfully

summary: Created mcp-server/src/storage/migrate-namespaced.ts implementing migrateToNamespacedLayout(ledgerRoot: string): Promise<MigrationResult>

Migration scans depth-1 dirs in ledgerRoot looking for .meta.json — flat-layout projects. For each, reads repository_name (falls back to 'unknown' if absent/null/empty) and moves to {ledgerRoot}/{repoName}/{slug}/
Idempotency: reads .migration-state.json; skips if storage_version >= 2
Sentinel file .migration-in-progress written before any moves, removed after (enables crash recovery — re-run is safe)
Individual move failures: original dir left untouched, error surfaced in result.errors; .migration-state.json NOT written (allows retry on next startup)
EXDEV cross-device rename fallback: recursive copy-then-delete with top-level verification
storage_version: 2 written to .migration-state.json only when errors.length === 0

Wired into mcp-server/src/index.ts: await migrateToNamespacedLayout(ledgerRoot) called after mkdirSync(ledgerRoot, { recursive: true }) and before readConfigFromDisk(configPath), wrapped in try/catch to prevent fatal startup errors

Created mcp-server/tests/storage/migrate-namespaced.test.ts with 10 tests: clean run, unknown/ fallbacks (absent/null/empty), idempotent second run, state file content, sentinel cleanup, already-namespaced ledger, move-failure preserves original, crash-resume partial migration. All 10 pass.

comments.note: migrate-namespaced.ts: verifyDirCopied() only checks the top-level entries of src exist in dest, not recursively. For deeply-nested project dirs, a partial copy failure in a sub-dir would not be caught. Consider recursive verification or computing a recursive file count. Low priority since EXDEV cross-device renames are rare in practice (ledger root and temp dirs typically on the same filesystem).

index.ts: The migration catch block swallows errors silently (logs to stderr then continues startup). Consider whether a migration failure that leaves the storage layout partially migrated should block startup or emit a more prominent warning. Acceptable tradeoff for now since partial migration is resumable.

summary: Reviewed migrate-namespaced.ts (migrateToNamespacedLayout), migrate-namespaced.test.ts (10 tests), and index.ts startup wiring. One Fix-Forward applied: expanded verifyDirCopied() docstring to clarify why shallow verification is sufficient given that copyDirRecursive() throws on any failure. Implementation correctly follows the sentinel-file crash-recovery pattern, EXDEV cross-device fallback, and non-fatal startup error handling. All 6 ACs met. No blocking issues.

comments.note: verifyDirCopied() docstring was ambiguous about why shallow (non-recursive) verification is sufficient — expanded comment to explain that copyDirRecursive() already propagates all errors via await, making deep re-verification redundant. Non-behavioral docstring change.

verifyDirCopied() only checks top-level entry existence via access(). This is correct (see Fix-Forward comment above) but worth noting: if a zero-byte copy were somehow possible (e.g., disk quota exhausted mid-write but copyFile returned), the verification would not catch corrupted file content. This scenario is extremely unlikely in practice and acceptable for a migration utility.

Sentinel file is written with writeFile() (not atomicWriteJson). If the process crashes after writeFile() but before any rename(), the next startup finds the sentinel and re-runs the migration loop. The loop is idempotent (already-moved dirs skipped via dirExists). This is correct and intentional — the sentinel serves as a crash-recovery signal, not a data file.

[documentation-forward] constraints.md should document the 'unknown' namespace collision scenario at the migration layer: if a user has a repository literally named 'unknown', projects from that repo AND projects with invalid/absent repository_name will share the {ledgerRoot}/unknown/ namespace, and slug collisions may occur. Add to Known Limitations alongside the LedgerStore.storageDir 'unknown' limitation from WP-002.
